Cold Metal Transfer Welding of Dissimilar Metals/Alloys

Contact:

Abstract:

The role of processes parameters, such as applied current, voltage and travel speed during welding of two dissimilar alloys, e.g. Kovar alloy and stainless steel 302L, through cold metal transfer (CMT) welding has been investigated. Variation in welding parameters showed a substantial influence on weld bead morphology, phase formation, and mechanical properties. The weld pool size was observed to be increase as a function of heat input during welding.&nbsp The fusion zone (FZ) has a predominantly dendritic structure in all conditions of welding. Micro-hardness in the FZ was observed to higher than the Kovar alloy although it was much lower than the hardness of SS302L. Tensile testing showed SS302L possessed the highest strength (UTS 878.9 MPa), while Kovar exhibited superior ductility (elongation 34.58%). Welded joints displayed intermediate properties closely approaching to the tensile values of SS302L. Optimized parameters demonstrated mechanical performance comparable to stainless steel while ensuring compatibility with Kovar confirming CMT as an effective method for joining dissimilar metals and alloys. As a result, the invention offers a dependable and effective method for creating dissimilar joints between Kovar alloy and Stainless Steel 302L, increasing their use in crucial engineering domains like advanced manufacturing systems, electronics, nuclear industries, and aerospace.
